title: Barbershop hero and proof - benchmark examples
subtitle: Meikigo /barbershop hero and proof against Fresha, Square, Toast, Booksy, Squire and StoreHub homepages, captured live on 2026-09-28.
summary: The hero trails the market: every peer shows product or proof in the fold, Meikigo shows only a barber photo.
Strong pages put a verifiable number or rating next to the headline and name the audience in the H1 or sub.
Peers pair the main CTA with a softer path: an overview video, or WhatsApp chat in Malaysia (StoreHub).

recommendations.title: The product owns the fold
recommendations.why: A cold visitor knows it is software in one glance. Fresha, Squire and StoreHub fill half the hero with real screens, not a lifestyle photo.
how: Put the tablet queue board and the phone booking #42 screen in the hero, framed as devices.
Keep a barbershop photo only as background context behind the devices, not instead of them.
Reuse the screens already built for the three-screens section so no new design work is needed.

recommendations.title: A checkable number sits next to the headline
recommendations.why: StoreHub puts a Google rating above its H1, Toast names 180,000 locations in the sub. The proof lands before the visitor reads the pitch.
how: Do not invent a count. Collect Google Business Profile reviews first, then show the real rating above the H1.
Until then, use a factual line such as the RM109 price floor or supported payment rails as the proof slot.

recommendations.title: The H1 or sub names who it is for and why it differs
recommendations.why: Booksy names barbers, stylists and salon owners. Squire says the only POS built for barbers, solo or whole crew. Readers self-select in seconds.
how: Name barbershops and unisex salons, from one chair to multi-outlet, in the sub.
State the difference from booking apps in one line: booking, queue, payment and report on one tablet.

recommendations.title: A softer second action beside the main CTA
recommendations.why: Fresha pairs Get started with Watch an overview. StoreHub pairs its demo with Chat on WhatsApp, the channel Malaysian owners already use.
how: Add a Chat on WhatsApp button next to Start free, styled as secondary.
Or add a 60-second queue walkthrough video as the secondary action.

recommendations.title: Testimonials a visitor can verify
recommendations.why: Booksy shows video quotes with a real name, social handle and a link to the pro's live booking profile, then review-site ratings below.
how: Replace the current quotes only with real pilot shops that agree to be named, with a photo or short clip.
Link each quote to the shop's live Meikigo booking page or Google profile.
Until pilots sign off, drop the section rather than show unverified names.

working: One CTA label, Start free, with no card and no contract right under it. Stronger risk reduction than Square or Toast.
Transparent RM pricing on the page. Toast and Square push demos or sales contact first.
An honest compare against typical booking apps, a move only Toast makes among these peers.

references.title: Meikigo /barbershop hero (current)
references.caption: Current state, desktop 1440x900
references.insight: Photo-led fold with no product, no number, and a low-contrast trial line.

references.title: Fresha for business
references.caption: Calendar UI fills the fold under two CTAs
references.insight: Real desktop and phone calendar dominate the fold. Watch an overview sits beside Get started as the soft path.

references.title: SQUIRE homepage
references.caption: Three phone screens under a barber-only claim
references.insight: Sub says the only POS built for barbers, solo or whole crew. Booking, barber and reports screens show every side.

references.title: StoreHub Malaysia
references.caption: Rating above H1, devices left, WhatsApp as second CTA
references.insight: Local peer. 4.7/5 from 2,200+ Google reviews sits above the H1, and Chat on WhatsApp is the secondary action.

references.title: Toast POS
references.caption: Customer count in the sub, logo strip under the fold
references.insight: Trusted by 180,000 locations sits inside the sub. A video pill above the H1 offers the low-commitment path.

references.title: Booksy Biz
references.caption: H1 names barbers, stylists and salon owners
references.insight: The H1 is the audience. The sub adds every feature on every plan and 330,000+ pros, then one CTA.

references.title: Booksy testimonials
references.caption: Video quotes with handles and profile links, ratings below
references.insight: Each quote has a name, social handle and a link to the pro's live profile. Review-site ratings follow directly.

references.title: Square Appointments
references.caption: Short outcome H1, device in real use below
references.insight: Plain outcome H1 and a real counter tablet in use. Two CTAs compete at similar weight, a move to avoid.
